newsitem.title: UK: Mark firm on crosses but trapped in range.
newsitem.headline: Mark firm on crosses but trapped in range.

text.p: The mark was firm on its European crosses on Tuesday but remained trapped within intraday ranges during afternoon trade.
The Swedish crown continued to hover around session lows against the mark after the announcement of Sweden's budget, trading at 4.4365/95 at 1400 GMT compared with 4.4295/25 late on Monday.

Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson's budget outlined a five-point spending plan, and proposed spending 5.5 billion crowns for labour market and growth measures in 1997, 16.3 billion in 1998, 21.0 billion in 1999 and 23.3 billion in 2000.

Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said the government's budget spending ceiling would remain unchanged for 1997, 1998 and 1999, and added the spending ceiling for the year 2000 would be set at 744 billion crowns.
Swedish unemployment would fall below 4.5 percent in 2000, the government added. It had previously pledged to bring unemployment below 4.0 percent.
The mark shrugged off an EMU-negative European Monetary Institute (EMI) annual report, analysts said.

"The EMI has fired a warning shot to tell the markets that a lot of work is still to be done but the report didn't contain much to change the overall market view on EMU," said Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Commerzbank.

The EMI, forerunner of the European central bank, expressed serious concerns that many European Union states have not yet managed to rein in their national deficits enough to launch the single currency in 1999.
This comes after six leading economic institutes on Sunday said Germany would miss the European Monetary Union (EMU) three percent budget deficit target.

"Anything that suggests the German budget deficit is overshooting will be perceived by the markets as increasing the likelihood of a broad-based EMU," Bank America chief economist Jeremy Hawkins said.

The lira continued to bounce off support around 982, but would find it difficult to continue appreciating given Italy's weak GDP data yesterday and this morning's industrial production numbers, BZW currency strategist Chris Turner said.
"We remain sceptical about Italy's ability to qualify for EMU," he added.
Italian industrial output fell 3.8 percent year-on-year in February against forecasts for a 2.3 percent drop.
Mark/lira was trading at 983.40/3.70 against 983.35/85 on Monday.

The peseta was slightly weaker against the mark at 84.20/4.22 against 84.14 at the previous close after profit-taking followed a widely-expected repo rate cut by the Bank of Spain to 5.50 percent from 5.75 percent.
The rate cut comes after benign March inflation data, released last week, which showed inflation dropping to 2.2 percent, the lowest level in nearly 30 years.

Dealers said the rate cut was likely to lend support to the peseta but that it was under profit-taking pressure after its rise to 10-week highs at 84.08 on Monday. -- Simon Gardner, London Newsroom + 44 171 542 6762
